samples.input:
Use a surfaceId of 'main'. Generate a 'createSurface' message to describe the following UI:

A vertical list with:
- Dog breed information
- Dog generator

The dog breed information is a card, which contains a title “Famous Dog breeds”, a header image, and a horizontal list of images of different dog breeds (using a 'List' component). The list information should be in the data model at /breeds.

The dog generator is another card which is a form that generates a fictional dog breed with a description
- Title
- Description text explaining what it is
- Dog breed name (text input)
- Number of legs (number input)
- Button called “Generate” which takes the data above and generates a new dog description
- Skills (ChoicePicker component, variant 'multipleSelection')
- A divider
- A section which shows the generated content
samples.target: A valid A2UI payload with surfaceId 'main' . The UI must include a vertical list with a 'Famous Dog breeds' card (header image, horizontal list of breeds) and a 'Dog generator' card (form with Title, Description, name input, legs input, 'Generate' button, skills ChoicePicker, and result section).

messages.content:
You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
Output the user interface using compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.

- (AudioPlayer :url :description? :weight?)
  - :url: The URL of the audio to be played.
  - :description: A description of the audio, such as a title or summary.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Button :child :variant? :action :weight? :checks?)
  - :child: The ID of the child component. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button. Only use an 'Icon' if the requirements explicitly ask for an icon-only button. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :variant: A hint for the button style. If omitted, a default button style is used. 'primary' indicates this is the main call-to-action button. 'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (Card :child :weight?)
  - :child: The ID of the single child component to be rendered inside the card. To display multiple elements, you MUST wrap them in a layout component (like Column or Row) and pass that container's ID here. Do NOT pass multiple IDs or a non-existent ID. Do NOT define the child component inline.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.
- (CheckBox :label :value :weight? :checks?)
  - :label: The text to display next to the checkbox.

content.summary:
**UI Construction Plan: My Thought Process**

Alright, let's break this down step-by-step. My objective is to build a UI as specified, and I need to do so following the strict guidelines.  The UI needs to be rendered on `surfaceId` 'main', with a root component 'root'.  The structure will be a `Column` containing two primary `Card` components: one for dog breed information, and another for a fictional dog breed generator.

First, I define the key components and their data sources. I'll need a `/breeds` data structure containing image URLs and breed names.  I'll initialize it with a few example breeds, for instance: `[(:url "...") (:url "...") (:url "...")]`. Then, for the generator, I'll set up form variables for breed name (`$/form/breedName`), number of legs (`$/form/legs`, defaulting to 4), and skills (`$/form/skills`, an array).  I'll also define the available skills as an array: `["Super Jump", "Telepathy", ...]`.

Next, I think about data binding and how I'll handle the "Generate" button's action.  It needs to trigger an event, which I'll call "generate_breed". I can then bind the form input values to the generated output. I'll also use `formatString` to create dynamic descriptions of the generated breed in the output section. I'll also initialize the root data using the `data` component.

The critical bit here is the component tree and nesting. I must carefully obey the rules, which dictate that everything has to be nested and follow the example:
`(Column :children [(Card :child (Column ...))])`.

No flat lists! I'll build the component tree directly, constructing the nested structure carefully, adhering to the "You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions" rule.

The first card, "Dog Breed Information," will contain a title, a header image, and a horizontal `List` of breed images.  Each list item will contain a simple `Column` with an image and breed name.

The second card, the generator, is the form component. It'll consist of a title, a description, text fields for the breed name and number of legs, a `ChoicePicker` for skills, and a "Generate" button that triggers an action.  A divider will separate the input fields from the output section, which will display the generated breed's information using formatted text (using `formatString`).

I'll then refine the initialization of the state using the `data` component, making sure all data paths are properly initialized and ready.

Format checks:
I must make sure that there are no custom style attributes and that all components are nested according to the rules (inline or using `:children` properties).
I need to check that the UI structure has exactly one root component with `:id "root"` (which has to be a `Column`).

I need to make sure that Button uses `Text` as a child and that card uses column as a child.

Finally, I'll go through a final validation of the structure and visual requirements to be sure that I have all the components and the constraints are followed.

After this check, I'll produce the final S-expression.

content.text:
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root" :children [
  (data
    $/breeds [
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1?w=200" :name "Golden Retriever")
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1583511655857-d19b40a7a54e?w=200" :name "Poodle")
      (:url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1537151625747-768eb6cf92b2?w=200" :name "Husky")
    ]
    $/skills_list ["Super Jump" "Telepathy" "Laser Eyes" "Sonic Bark" "Infinite Appetite"]
    $/form/name "Robo-Pug"
    $/form/legs 4
    $/form/skills ["Super Jump" "Laser Eyes"]
  )
  (Card :child
    (Column :children [
      (Text :text "Famous Dog breeds" :variant "body")
      (Image :url "https://images.unsplash.com/photo-1543466835-00a7907e9de1?w=600" :description "Famous Dog Breeds Banner" :variant "header")
      (List :direction "horizontal" :children
        (template :item breed
          (Column :children [
            (Image :url $/breed/url :description $/breed/name :variant "smallFeature")
            (Text :text $/breed/name :variant "caption")
          ])
        )
      )
    ])
  )
  (Card :child
    (Column :children [
      (Text :text "Fictional Dog Breed Generator" :variant "body")
      (Text :text "Create your own custom fictional dog breed by choosing its attributes below!" :variant "caption")
      (TextField :label "Dog Breed Name" :value $/form/name :variant "shortText")
      (TextField :label "Number of Legs" :value $/form/legs :variant "number")
      (ChoicePicker :label "Special Skills" :variant "multipleSelection" :options $/skills_list :value $/form/skills :displayStyle "chips")
      (Button :child (Text :text "Generate") :variant "primary" :action (Event "generate_dog" :name $/form/name :legs $/form/legs :skills $/form/skills))
      (Divider :axis "horizontal")
      (Column :children [
        (Text :text "Generated Concept:" :variant "body")
        (Text :text (formatString "Meet the amazing ${/form/name}! A unique breed with ${/form/legs} legs, known for special skills: ${/form/skills}.") :variant "caption")
      ])
    ])
  )
])
</a2ui>

content.summary:
**Login Form UI Construction: A Step-by-Step Thought Process**

Alright, let's break this down. My goal is to craft a login form UI, and it needs to be perched on the 'main' surface with a root component identified as 'root'. No problem. First, let's get the elements sorted. I see a title, username and password fields, a "Remember Me" checkbox, and a "Sign In" button.

The title, a "# Login" heading, seems like a job for the `Text` component. It supports Markdown, so that's the path I'll take, making it easy to style. Username and Password will be `TextField` components with the `:label` and appropriate `:variant` attributes. I'll bind the values to data paths, `/login/username` and `/login/password` respectively. The "Remember Me" checkbox is a straightforward `CheckBox` component bound to `/login/rememberMe`.

Now, the button. The catalog says a button needs a child component. And the prompt is very strict about nesting components. "Do NOT define the child component inline. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button". That's a little confusing, but looking at the S-expression, that means the `Text` component *is* going inline under the `:child` attribute, and it is *not* a string directly: `(Button :child (Text :text "Sign In") ...)`. It is nested, *not* defined elsewhere via IDs.

Now for the Sign In action. The specification says there should be an event named "login" with a context that contains username, password, and rememberMe. My instinct is that `:action (Event "login" :username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe)` covers it. However, the requirement specifically calls for "a 'context' containing...", so I will construct the action event with a nested context parameter: `:action (Event "login" :context (:username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe))`. I have to be precise; a map is created as `(:key1 val1 :key2 val2)`, and the grammar allows it.

The root component requires focus. It must have an `id: 'root'`. The system wants "one root component with id: 'root'" and "Do NOT output ... explicit :id attributes..." So, I will add `:id "root"` to the outermost `Column` component, assuming this explicitly satisfies the requirement for the root ID. But, I am careful to not add this to any other component, as this would violate the rules.

Since this system needs data initialization, the first element nested in the root will be `(data $/login/username "" $/login/password "" $/login/rememberMe false)`. This should set up the initial state of the data model.

The complete tree looks like this (with the root):

```lisp
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/login/username "" $/login/password "" $/login/rememberMe false)
  (Text :text "# Login")
  (TextField :label "Username" :value $/login/username :variant "shortText")
  (TextField :label "Password" :value $/login/password :variant "obscured")
  (CheckBox :label "Remember Me" :value $/login/rememberMe)
  (Button :child (Text :text "Sign In")
          :variant "primary"
          :action (Event "login" :context (:username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe))))
</a2ui>
```

I re-read every component and its attributes. Everything seems correct, nested, and using allowed properties and no "invented" attributes, matching the grammar and constraints precisely.

**Login Form UI Construction: A Step-by-Step Thought Process**

Alright, let's break this down. My goal is to craft a login form UI, and it needs to be perched on the 'main' surface with a root component identified as 'root'. No problem. First, let's get the elements sorted. I see a title, username and password fields, a "Remember Me" checkbox, and a "Sign In" button.

The title, a "# Login" heading, seems like a job for the `Text` component. It supports Markdown, so that's the path I'll take, making it easy to style. Username and Password will be `TextField` components with the `:label` and appropriate `:variant` attributes. I'll bind the values to data paths, `/login/username` and `/login/password` respectively. The "Remember Me" checkbox is a straightforward `CheckBox` component bound to `/login/rememberMe`.

Now, the button. The catalog says a button needs a child component. And the prompt is very strict about nesting components. "Do NOT define the child component inline. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button". That's a little confusing, but looking at the S-expression, that means the `Text` component *is* going inline under the `:child` attribute, and it is *not* a string directly: `(Button :child (Text :text "Sign In") ...)`. It is nested, *not* defined elsewhere via IDs.

Now for the Sign In action. The specification says there should be an event named "login" with a context that contains username, password, and rememberMe. My instinct is that `:action (Event "login" :username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe)` covers it. However, the requirement specifically calls for "a 'context' containing...", so I will construct the action event with a nested context parameter: `:action (Event "login" :context (:username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe))`. I have to be precise; a map is created as `(:key1 val1 :key2 val2)`, and the grammar allows it.

The root component requires focus. It must have an `id: 'root'`. The system wants "one root component with id: 'root'" and "Do NOT output ... explicit :id attributes..." So, I will add `:id "root"` to the outermost `Column` component, assuming this explicitly satisfies the requirement for the root ID. But, I am careful to not add this to any other component, as this would violate the rules.

Since this system needs data initialization, the first element nested in the root will be `(data $/login/username "" $/login/password "" $/login/rememberMe false)`. This should set up the initial state of the data model.

The complete tree looks like this (with the root):

```lisp
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/login/username "" $/login/password "" $/login/rememberMe false)
  (Text :text "# Login")
  (TextField :label "Username" :value $/login/username :variant "shortText")
  (TextField :label "Password" :value $/login/password :variant "obscured")
  (CheckBox :label "Remember Me" :value $/login/rememberMe)
  (Button :child (Text :text "Sign In")
          :variant "primary"
          :action (Event "login" :context (:username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe))))
</a2ui>
```

I re-read every component and its attributes. Everything seems correct, nested, and using allowed properties and no "invented" attributes, matching the grammar and constraints precisely.

You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
Output the user interface using compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.

- (AudioPlayer :url :description? :weight?)

  - :description: A description of the audio, such as a title or summary.
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'

Alright, let's break this down. My goal is to craft a login form UI, and it needs to be perched on the 'main' surface with a root component identified as 'root'. No problem. First, let's get the elements sorted. I see a title, username and password fields, a "Remember Me" checkbox, and a "Sign In" button.

The title, a "# Login" heading, seems like a job for the `Text` component. It supports Markdown, so that's the path I'll take, making it easy to style. Username and Password will be `TextField` components with the `:label` and appropriate `:variant` attributes. I'll bind the values to data paths, `/login/username` and `/login/password` respectively. The "Remember Me" checkbox is a straightforward `CheckBox` component bound to `/login/rememberMe`.

Now, the button. The catalog says a button needs a child component. And the prompt is very strict about nesting components. "Do NOT define the child component inline. Use a 'Text' component for a labeled button". That's a little confusing, but looking at the S-expression, that means the `Text` component *is* going inline under the `:child` attribute, and it is *not* a string directly: `(Button :child (Text :text "Sign In") ...)`. It is nested, *not* defined elsewhere via IDs.

Now for the Sign In action. The specification says there should be an event named "login" with a context that contains username, password, and rememberMe. My instinct is that `:action (Event "login" :username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe)` covers it. However, the requirement specifically calls for "a 'context' containing...", so I will construct the action event with a nested context parameter: `:action (Event "login" :context (:username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe))`. I have to be precise; a map is created as `(:key1 val1 :key2 val2)`, and the grammar allows it.

The root component requires focus. It must have an `id: 'root'`. The system wants "one root component with id: 'root'" and "Do NOT output ... explicit :id attributes..." So, I will add `:id "root"` to the outermost `Column` component, assuming this explicitly satisfies the requirement for the root ID. But, I am careful to not add this to any other component, as this would violate the rules.

Since this system needs data initialization, the first element nested in the root will be `(data $/login/username "" $/login/password "" $/login/rememberMe false)`. This should set up the initial state of the data model.

The complete tree looks like this (with the root):

```lisp
<a2ui>
(Column :id "root"
  (data $/login/username "" $/login/password "" $/login/rememberMe false)
  (Text :text "# Login")
  (TextField :label "Username" :value $/login/username :variant "shortText")
  (TextField :label "Password" :value $/login/password :variant "obscured")
  (CheckBox :label "Remember Me" :value $/login/rememberMe)
  (Button :child (Text :text "Sign In")
          :variant "primary"
          :action (Event "login" :context (:username $/login/username :password $/login/password :rememberMe $/login/rememberMe))))
</a2ui>
```

I re-read every component and its attributes. Everything seems correct, nested, and using allowed properties and no "invented" attributes, matching the grammar and constraints precisely.

You are an AI assistant. Based on the following request, generate a user interface.

## Instructions:
Output the user interface using compact A2UI Atom S-Expression notation.
You MUST surround the entire A2UI Atom block with sentinel tags `<a2ui>` and `</a2ui>`. Do NOT output raw JSON messages.

## Grammar Rules

1. Every component node is a parenthesized expression starting with the ComponentName:
   (ComponentName :key1 val1 :key2 val2 child1 child2 ...)

2. Primitives:
   - Strings: Double-quoted, e.g., "Hello". Escapes: \n, \t, \\, \".
   - Numbers: Integers or decimals, e.g., 42 or 3.14.
   - Booleans: true or false.
   - Null: null.

3. Property Arguments:
   - Tagged attributes: Prefixed with a colon ':', e.g., :attr1 "val1" or :attr2 true. Tagged keys are order-independent.
   - Positional attributes: Can be passed sequentially matching catalog signature order.

4. Child Components & Strict Tree Nesting:
   - You MUST nest child components directly inside their parent container expressions, e.g., (ContainerComponent (ChildComponent (PrimitiveComponent "Hello"))).
   - Do NOT output flat adjacency lists, explicit `:id` attributes, or separate component variable IDs. Every UI component must be nested directly within a single root tree expression.

5. Data Bindings:
   - Absolute data model paths start with '$/', e.g., $/user/firstName.
   - Relative template item fields start with '$/item_var/field', e.g. $/item/name.

6. Data Model Population:
   - Initialize data model state using (data $/path1 "val1" $/path2 123) or (data $/map_path (:key1 "val1" :key2 "val2")).

7. Dynamic List Templates:
   - List templates use (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name)) or (ListComponent :children (template :item item (ChildComponent $/item/name))).

8. Action Events:
   - Actions use (Event "action_name" :param1 $/value). Interactive controls with action attributes MUST provide an action expression, e.g., (ActionComponent :child (ChildComponent "Text") :action (Event "click_action")).

9. Standalone Operations:
   - Delete surface: (deleteSurface "surface_id")
   - Call RPC function: (callFunction "function_name" :arg1 "value1")

10. Syntax Structure Examples (Abstract Grammar):
   Example 1 (Container with Child Nodes & Actions):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (ChildComponent :title "Header")
     (InputComponent :label "Input" :value $/form/field)
     (ActionComponent :label "Submit" :action (Event "submit_action" :val $/form/field)))
   </a2ui>

   Example 2 (Root Data State & Dynamic Template):
   <a2ui>
   (ContainerComponent
     (data $/items [(:id 1 :name "Item 1")] $/title "List Title")
     (ListComponent :items $/items :template (template item (ChildComponent :title $/item/name))))
   </a2ui>

11. Strict Catalog Adherence & Conciseness:
   - You MUST ONLY use property names listed in the Component Catalog Signatures below.
   - Do NOT invent CSS or style attributes (e.g. style, padding, margin, backgroundColor, color, fontSize, size, minHeight, borderRadius, spacing, align, justify).
   - Output minimal properties required to satisfy the user request.



Additional Rules:
1. Construct the user interface on surfaceId 'main'.
2. If components are defined, ensure there is one root component with id: 'root'.

  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

'borderless' means the button has no visual border or background, making its child content appear like a clickable link. Must be one of: 'default', 'primary', 'borderless'
  - :weight: The relative weight of this component within a Row or Column. This is similar to the CSS 'flex-grow' property. Note: this may ONLY be set when the component is a direct descendant of a Row or Column.

<a2ui>
(Column :id "root" :children [
  (data $/profile/name "Jane Doe" $/notifications/emailEnabled true)
  (Text :text "User Settings" :variant "body")
  (Tabs :tabs [
    (:title "Profile" :child (Column :children [
      (TextField :label "Name" :value $/profile/name :variant "shortText")
    ]))
    (:title "# Notifications" :child (Column :children [
      (CheckBox :label "Enable email notifications" :value $/notifications/emailEnabled)
    ]))
  ])
  (Modal
    :trigger (Button :child (Text :text "Delete Account") :variant "default" :action (Event "open_delete_confirm"))
    :content (Column :children [
      (Text :text "Are you sure you want to delete your account? This action cannot be undone." :variant "body")
      (Row :children [
        (Button :child (Text :text "Confirm Deletion") :variant "primary" :action (Event "confirm_delete"))
        (Button :child (Text :text "Cancel") :variant "default" :action (Event "cancel_delete"))
      ])
    ]))
])
</a2ui>
